title: Amenability Reiter Nets and Folner Conditions

items.title: Left-invariant means on L-infinity of a locally compact group
items.statement: Conventions for this page. $G$ is a locally compact Hausdorff group with a fixed left Haar measure $\mu$, and $L^\infty(G)=L^\infty(G,\mu;\mathbb C)$ is the space of equivalence classes of essentially bounded measurable functions with the essential-supremum norm ([[def-l-infinity-on-a-measure-space]]). For $g\in G$ the left translate is $L_gf(x):=f(g^{-1}x)$; it maps $L^\infty(G)$ into itself and is isometric, and $L_{g_1}L_{g_2}=L_{g_1g_2}$. A **mean** on $L^\infty(G)$ is a $\mathbb C$-linear $m:L^\infty(G)\to\mathbb C$ with $m(f)\ge0$ whenever $f\ge0$ and $m(1_G)=1$; equivalently a positive linear functional of norm one. It is **left invariant** when $m(L_gf)=m(f)$ for all $g\in G$, $f\in L^\infty(G)$. Every mean is bounded with $\lVert m\rVert=1$ and satisfies $|m(f)|\le m(|f|)\le\lVert f\rVert_\infty$.
items.strategy: Conventions item: every object named (Haar measure, $L^\infty(G)$, its classes and norm, the left translation action) is an already constructed published object, and the only substantive assertions are the isometry $\lVert L_gf\rVert_\infty=\lVert f\rVert_\infty$, the multiplicativity $L_{g_1}L_{g_2}=L_{g_1g_2}$, and the norm bound for a positive functional. The last is proved from positivity: $-\lVert f\rVert_\infty\mathbf 1_G\le f\le\lVert f\rVert_\infty\mathbf 1_G$ gives $|m(f)|\le\lVert f\rVert_\infty$ for real $f$; for complex $f$ apply this to the real and imaginary parts, and $m(|f|)\le\lVert f\rVert_\infty$ gives the displayed chain once $|m(f)|\le m(|f|)$ is noted for positive functionals.

items.title: Amenable locally compact group
items.statement: A locally compact Hausdorff group $G$ is **amenable** when there exists a left-invariant mean $m$ on $L^\infty(G)$ ([[def-left-invariant-mean-on-l-infinity-of-a-locally-compact-group]]): a positive $\mathbb C$-linear functional with $m(1_G)=1$ and $m(L_gf)=m(f)$ for all $g\in G$ and $f\in L^\infty(G)$. No countability, discreteness or unimodularity assumption is made; the left Haar measure is kept fixed but the property does not depend on its normalization.
items.strategy: Definition item. The only hidden content is normalization independence: rescaling $\mu$ rescales the $L^\infty$ norm but not the set of means, since the mean is a functional on classes and left invariance and positivity are normalization-free. Nonempty classes such as compact or abelian groups are treated later on this page.

items.title: Reiter's condition (P1)
items.statement: Let $\mathcal P:=\{f\in L^1(G):f\ge0,\ \lVert f\rVert_1=1\}$ and let $L_gf(x)=f(g^{-1}x)$. $G$ satisfies **Reiter's condition (P1)** when for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $f\in\mathcal P$ with $$\sup_{g\in Q}\lVert L_gf-f\rVert_1\le\varepsilon.$$ Equivalently (the net formulation) there is a net $(f_i)$ in $\mathcal P$ such that $\lVert L_gf_i-f_i\rVert_1\to0$ uniformly on compact subsets of $G$: for each compact $Q$ and $\varepsilon$ all sufficiently far out $f_i$ satisfy the displayed estimate. $\mathcal P$ is convex, and $L_g\mathcal P=\mathcal P$; the condition uses left translates and the fixed left Haar measure, with no compactness of $G$ assumed.
items.strategy: Conventions item for the analytic approximate-invariance condition. The equivalence of the two formulations is the usual passage between a net indexed by the directed set of pairs $(Q,\varepsilon)$ and an estimate uniform on compacta; convexity of $\mathcal P$ is additivity of the integral for nonnegative functions, and the left invariance $\lVert L_gf\rVert_1=\lVert f\rVert_1$ is left invariance of $\mu$. The right-hand statement that these estimates are exactly what the Reiter theorem needs is established by the later items of this page.

items.title: Left Folner nets for locally compact groups
items.statement: $G$ satisfies the **left Folner condition** when for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $\mu$-measurable set $F\subseteq G$ with $0<\mu(F)<\infty$ and $$\sup_{g\in Q}\frac{\mu(gF\mathbin\triangle F)}{\mu(F)}\le\varepsilon .$$ A **left Folner net** is a net $(F_i)$ of measurable sets of positive finite measure such that $\mu(gF_i\mathbin\triangle F_i)/\mu(F_i)\to0$ uniformly on compact subsets of $G$. Equivalently the condition holds with $Q$ ranging over the compact subsets; it suffices to test compact sets containing the identity. Only left translates $gF$ appear, and $\mu$ is left invariant.
items.strategy: Definition item. It records the two equivalent shapes (single test sets and nets) and the harmless reduction to compact sets containing $e$: for an arbitrary compact $Q$, apply the condition to $Q\cup\{e\}$. No proof obligation beyond these conventions; the equivalence with amenability is deferred to [[thm-folner-criterion-for-locally-compact-groups]].

items.title: Left-uniformly-continuous bounded functions (UCB)
items.statement: The space $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ consists of the classes $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$ for which the map $G\to L^\infty(G)$, $x\mapsto L_x\varphi$, is continuous, that is: for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a neighbourhood $V$ of $e$ with $\lVert L_x\varphi-\varphi\rVert_\infty<\varepsilon$ for all $x\in V$. Then $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ is a closed linear subspace of $L^\infty(G)$ containing the constants, it is $L_g$-invariant for every $g$, and the left translation action $G\times\mathrm{UCB}(G)\to\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ is continuous. If a $\mathrm{UCB}$-function vanishes almost everywhere then it vanishes identically, so $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ sits inside $L^\infty(G)$ as a genuine space of functions.
items.strategy: Definition with the basic closure facts. Closedness: uniform limits of translation-continuous functions are translation-continuous (an $\varepsilon/3$ argument on $\lVert L_x\varphi-\varphi\rVert_\infty$). Invariance and continuity of the action follow from $L_{x}L_g=L_{xg}$ and $\lVert L_x\psi-\psi\rVert_\infty=\lVert L_{x}\psi-L_{x'}\psi\rVert_\infty$ for $\psi=L_{x'}\varphi$. The injectivity assertion: if $\varphi=0$ a.e. and $\varphi\in\mathrm{UCB}(G)$, fix $t$ with $\varphi(t)=c\ne0$ and put $\psi=L_{t^{-1}}\varphi$; then $\psi(e)=c$, $\psi=0$ a.e., and translation continuity at $e$ gives $\lvert\psi(y)-c\rvert<\lvert c\rvert/2$ for $y$ in a neighbourhood of $e$, which has positive Haar measure, contradicting $\psi=0$ a.e.

items.title: Every locally compact Hausdorff group has an open sigma-compact subgroup
items.statement: Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group and let $U$ be a compact neighbourhood of $e$. Then the subgroup $H=\bigcup_{n\ge0}U^n$ generated by $U$ is open and $\sigma$-compact; in particular every locally compact Hausdorff group has an open $\sigma$-compact subgroup.
items.strategy: $H$ is a subgroup because $U$ may be taken symmetric (replace $U$ by $U\cup U^{-1}$) and $H$ is the union of the powers $U^n$. Each $U^n$ is compact, as the image of the compact product $U\times\dots\times U$ under the continuous multiplication map, so $H$ is a countable union of compact sets. For openness, choose a nonempty open $W\subseteq U$ and cover the compact set $U$ by finitely many translates $u_1W,\dots,u_mW$; then $U^n\subseteq\{u_1,\dots,u_m\}^n\cdot W^n$, and each translate of the open set $W^n$ is an open subset of $H$ contained in $H$, so every point of $U^n$ lies in an open subset of $H$; hence $H$ is open.

items.title: Positive-measure subsets of Haar measure contain finite positive-measure subsets
items.statement: Let $\mu$ be a left Haar measure on a locally compact Hausdorff group $G$. Then $\mu$ is semifinite: every Borel set $A$ with $\mu(A)>0$ contains a Borel subset $B$ with $0<\mu(B)<\infty$. For a $\mu$-measurable $A$ the same conclusion follows by applying the Borel statement to a Borel set differing from $A$ by a $\mu$-null set and using completeness of the Haar measure where present. No $\sigma$-compactness of $G$ is assumed; this is exactly the input used by the weak-star density of probability densities and by the averaging identity $\sup_{f\in\mathcal P}\int_Gfh\,d\mu=\lVert h\rVert_\infty$.
items.strategy:
Write $A$ measurable with $\mu(A)>0$; replacing $A$ by a Borel subset of full relative measure is not needed if one works with the completion, so fix a Borel $A$ and note the general case follows by the same argument applied to a Borel set differing from $A$ by a null set. Case 1: $\mu(A)<\infty$. Outer regularity of the Haar measure gives open $U\supseteq A$ with $\mu(U)<\mu(A)+\varepsilon$; inner regularity on open sets gives a compact $K\subseteq U$ with $\mu(K)>\mu(U)-\varepsilon$; since $\mu(U)$ is finite, $\mu(K\cap A)=\mu(K)-\mu(K\setminus A)\ge \mu(K)-(\mu(U)-\mu(A))>\mu(A)-2\varepsilon$, and taking $\varepsilon<\mu(A)/2$ gives the compact (hence finite-measure) $B:=K\cap A\subseteq A$ with $\mu(B)>0$. Case 2: $\mu(A)=\infty$. Fix an open $\sigma$-compact subgroup $H\le G$ ([[lem-an-lch-group-has-an-open-sigma-compact-subgroup]]); each coset $xH$ is open, the quotient $G/H$ is discrete, and a section $s:G/H	o G$ with $s(x)\in xH$ exists by choice. Define $
u(E):=\sum_{x\in G/H}\mu_H(s(x)^{-1}E\cap H)$ for Borel $E$, the sum taken as the supremum over finite partial sums. Then $
u$ is a nonzero left-invariant content, finite on compact sets (a compact set meets finitely many cosets and each slice is compact), hence extends to a left Haar measure; left invariance follows from $s(x)^{-1}g\in H$ iff $x$ is the coset of $g$, and from left invariance of $\mu_H$ after re-indexing $x\mapsto g^{-1}x$. By uniqueness of the left Haar measure up to scale, $
u=c\,\mu$ with $c>0$. If every compact subset of $A$ were $\mu$-null, then for every $x$ every compact subset $L\subseteq A_x:=\{h\in H:s(x)h\in A\}$ would satisfy $\mu(s(x)L)=0$, and $\mu|_{H}$ is a left Haar measure on $H$, so $\mu_H(L)=0$; since $H$ is $\sigma$-compact the trivial $\sigma$-finite argument then gives $\mu_H(A_x)=0$, hence $
u(A)=0$, hence $\mu(A)=0$, a contradiction. So some compact subset $K\subseteq A$ has $\mu(K)>0$, and $B:=K$ is finite positive. Both cases use only the regularity properties of the published Haar measure, uniqueness of Haar measure on $G$ and on the open subgroup $H$, and a choice of coset representatives.

items.title: Averages over probability densities attain the essential supremum
items.statement: Let $h\in L^\infty(G)$ be real-valued and let $\mathcal P=\{f\in L^1(G):f\ge0,\ \lVert f\rVert_1=1\}$. Then $$\sup_{f\in\mathcal P}\int_Gfh\,d\mu=\lVert h\rVert_\infty .$$ The same identity holds for complex-valued $h$ with $\lVert h\rVert_\infty$ replaced by $\lVert\operatorname{Re}h\rVert_\infty$ or $\lVert\operatorname{Im}h\rVert_\infty$ after separating real and imaginary parts.
items.strategy: The inequality $\le$ is $\int fh\le\lVert h\rVert_\infty\lVert f\rVert_1=\lVert h\rVert_\infty$. For the reverse fix $\delta>0$ and put $A=\{h>\lVert h\rVert_\infty-\delta\}$: this has positive measure, because otherwise $h\le\lVert h\rVert_\infty-\delta$ almost everywhere would contradict the defining property of the essential supremum. The semifiniteness lemma provides a measurable $B\subseteq A$ with $0<\mu(B)<\infty$, and then $f=\mu(B)^{-1}\mathbf 1_B\in\mathcal P$ satisfies $\int fh\ge\lVert h\rVert_\infty-\delta$. Varying $\delta$ gives the identity; the complex case follows by taking real parts of $fh$ and using $\operatorname{Re}\int fh=\int f\operatorname{Re}h$.

items.title: L1 probability densities are weak-star dense in the set of means
items.statement: Let $\mathcal P=\{f\in L^1(G):f\ge0,\ \lVert f\rVert_1=1\}$, viewed as a subset of $L^\infty(G)^*$ through $f\mapsto(\varphi\mapsto\int_Gf\varphi\,d\mu)$, and let $M$ be the set of all means on $L^\infty(G)$. Then $\mathcal P$ is weak-star dense in $M$: for every mean $m$, every finite list $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_k\in L^\infty(G)$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $f\in\mathcal P$ with $\lvert\int_Gf\varphi_j\,d\mu-m(\varphi_j)\rvert<\varepsilon$ for $j=1,\dots,k$. In particular every mean is a weak-star limit of a net from $\mathcal P$.
items.strategy: Fix $m,\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_k,\varepsilon$ and consider the linear map $\Phi:L^1(G)\to\mathbb R^{2k}$, $\Phi(f)=(\operatorname{Re}\int f\varphi_j,\operatorname{Im}\int f\varphi_j)_{j}$; the set $\Phi(\mathcal P)$ is convex. If $v=(\operatorname{Re}m(\varphi_j),\operatorname{Im}m(\varphi_j))_j$ were outside its closure, strict separation in $\mathbb R^{2k}$ would give a nonzero linear functional $\ell$ on $\mathbb R^{2k}$ with $\ell(v)>\sup_{f\in\mathcal P}\ell(\Phi(f))$. Writing $\ell(\Phi(f))=\operatorname{Re}\int_G fh\,d\mu$ for the bounded measurable function $h=\sum_j(\lambda_j\varphi_j)$ determined by $\ell$, the averaging lemma gives $\sup_{f\in\mathcal P}\operatorname{Re}\int_Gfh\,d\mu=\lVert\operatorname{Re}h\rVert_\infty$. On the other hand $m$ is a mean, so $m(\operatorname{Re}h)$ is real, nonnegative on positive functions and satisfies $m(\operatorname{Re}h)\le\lVert\operatorname{Re}h\rVert_\infty$; and $\operatorname{Re}m(h)=m(\operatorname{Re}h)$ by complex linearity. Hence $\operatorname{Re}m(h)\le\lVert\operatorname{Re}h\rVert_\infty=\sup_{f\in\mathcal P}\operatorname{Re}\int_Gfh\,d\mu$ and the strict inequality is impossible. Therefore $v$ lies in the closure of $\Phi(\mathcal P)$ and some $f\in\mathcal P$ meets all $k$ coordinate estimates simultaneously; nets indexed by finite lists and tolerances then approximate each weak-star neighbourhood of $m$.

items.title: L1-convolution smooths bounded functions into UCB
items.statement: For $f\in L^1(G)$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$ define the convolution $(f*\varphi)(x):=\int_Gf(y)\varphi(y^{-1}x)\,d\mu(y)$. Then $f*\varphi$ is a bounded measurable function with $\lVert f*\varphi\rVert_\infty\le\lVert f\rVert_1\lVert\varphi\rVert_\infty$, its class lies in $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$, and for the left translates one has the quantitative bound $\lVert L_{g}(f*\varphi)-f*\varphi\rVert_\infty\le\lVert L_{g}f-f\rVert_1\lVert\varphi\rVert_\infty$. Moreover $*$ is bilinear on $L^1(G)\times L^\infty(G)$ and $L_g(f*\varphi)=(L_gf)*\varphi=f*(L_g\varphi)$.
items.strategy: Boundedness and measurability come from the iterated integral definition and Fubini-Tonelli for the integrand $\lvert f(y)\rvert\lVert\varphi\rVert_\infty$; the sup-norm estimate is immediate. For the translation bound write $L_g(f*\varphi)-f*\varphi=(L_gf)*\varphi-f*\varphi=(L_gf-f)*\varphi$ and apply the sup-norm estimate; bilinearity is linearity of the integral, and the intertwining identities follow by left invariance of $\mu$. That the class is in $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ then follows from the strong continuity of $g\mapsto L_gf$ on $L^1(G)$ and from density of $C_c(G)$ in $L^1(G)$ together with the sup-norm bound, which lets the estimate be verified first for continuous compactly supported $f$.

items.title: A UCB-invariant mean yields a topological invariant mean
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $m$ be a left-invariant mean on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$, i.e. a positive linear functional with $m(1_G)=1$ and $m(L_g\psi)=m(\psi)$ for all $\psi\in\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ and $g\in G$. Fix $f_0\in\mathcal P$ and define $\widetilde m(\varphi):=m(f_0*\varphi)$ for $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$. Then $\widetilde m$ is a mean on $L^\infty(G)$ and it is **topologically invariant**: $\widetilde m(f*\varphi)=\widetilde m(\varphi)$ for every $f\in\mathcal P$ and every $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$.
items.strategy: First, $m(f*\psi)=m(\psi)$ for every $f\in\mathcal P$ and $\psi\in\mathrm{UCB}(G)$: the map $y\mapsto L_{y^{-1}}\psi$ is continuous and bounded on the support of $f$, so $f*\psi=\int_Gf(y)(L_{y^{-1}}\psi)\,d\mu(y)$ is a Bochner integral in the Banach space $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$; applying the continuous linear functional $m$ and using left invariance termwise gives $m(f*\psi)=\int f(y)m(\psi)d\mu(y)=m(\psi)$. Choose the net $(f_i)\subseteq\mathcal P$ of the contractively bounded approximate identity with $\operatorname{supp}f_i\to\{e\}$; for $f,f'\in\mathcal P$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$ the identity above applied to $\psi=f*\varphi\in\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ gives $m(f*f_i*\varphi)=m(f*\varphi)$ and $\lVert f*f_i*\varphi-f*\varphi\rVert_\infty\le\lVert f_i*\varphi-\varphi\rVert_\infty\to0$, so $m(f*\varphi)=\lim_im(f_i*\varphi)=m(f'*\varphi)$. Hence $f_0*\varphi$ and $f*\varphi$ have the same $m$-value. Positivity and $\widetilde m(1_G)=m(f_0*1_G)=m(1_G)=1$ hold because convolution against the probability density $f_0$ preserves nonnegativity and constants; finally $\widetilde m(f*\varphi)=m(f_0*f*\varphi)=m(f_0*\varphi)=\widetilde m(\varphi)$.

items.title: A topological invariant mean yields norm-approximately invariant densities
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $\widetilde m$ be a topological invariant mean on $L^\infty(G)$: a mean with $\widetilde m(f*\varphi)=\widetilde m(\varphi)$ for all $f\in\mathcal P$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$. Then there is a net $(g_j)\subseteq\mathcal P$ such that $\lVert f*g_j-g_j\rVert_1\to0$ for every $f\in\mathcal P$, and this convergence is uniform on norm-compact subsets of $\mathcal P$: for every norm-compact $C\subseteq\mathcal P$ and every $\delta>0$ there is $j$ with $\sup_{f\in C}\lVert f*g_j-g_j\rVert_1<\delta$.
items.strategy: By the density lemma choose a net $(f_i)\subseteq\mathcal P$ with $\int f_i\psi\to\widetilde m(\psi)$ for every $\psi\in L^\infty(G)$. For fixed $f\in\mathcal P$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$, the adjoint identity for convolution on the left Haar measure gives $\int(f*f_i)\varphi\,d\mu=\int f_i(\widetilde f*\varphi)\,d\mu$ with $\widetilde f(y)=f(y^{-1})\Delta_G(y)$; since $\widetilde f\in\mathcal P$, topological invariance yields $\lim_i\int(f*f_i)\varphi=\widetilde m(\widetilde f*\varphi)=\widetilde m(\varphi)=\lim_i\int f_i\varphi$, so $f*f_i-f_i\to0$ weakly in $L^1(G)$. For a finite list $f_1,\dots,f_n$ the vector $(f_1*f_i-f_i,\dots,f_n*f_i-f_i)$ tends weakly to $0$ in the normed space $(L^1(G))^n$ with the max norm, so Mazur's theorem puts $0$ in the norm closure of the convex hull of any tail; a finite convex combination of the $f_i$ therefore gives $g\in\mathcal P$ with all $n$ norms below $\delta$, and a net indexed by finite lists and $\delta$ gives the first assertion. For a norm-compact $C$ choose a finite $\delta/3$-net $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_n$, apply the result to this list with tolerance $\delta/3$, and estimate $\lVert f*g-g\rVert_1\le\lVert f-\xi_k\rVert_1\lVert g\rVert_1+\lVert\xi_k*g-g\rVert_1$.

items.title: An invariant mean produces a Reiter net
items.statement: Assume AC. Suppose $G$ admits a left-invariant mean on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$; this holds in particular when $G$ is amenable in the sense of [[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]. Then $G$ satisfies Reiter's condition (P1) ([[def-reiter-condition-p1]]). Consequently every amenable locally compact group satisfies (P1).
items.strategy: Given a compact $Q$ containing $e$ and $\varepsilon>0$, pass from the left-invariant mean on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ to the topological invariant mean $\widetilde m$ of [[lem-a-ucb-invariant-mean-yields-a-topological-invariant-mean]], choose the net $(g_j)$ of [[lem-a-topological-invariant-mean-yields-norm-approximately-invariant-densities]], and fix $f\in\mathcal P$. By strong continuity the set $\{L_xf:x\in Q\}$ is norm compact in $L^1(G)$, so there is $j$ with $\lVert(L_xf)*g_j-g_j\rVert_1<\varepsilon/2$ for all $x\in Q$. Put $g:=f*g_j\in\mathcal P$ and use $L_x(f*g_j)=(L_xf)*g_j$ together with the case $x=e$ to get $\lVert L_xg-g\rVert_1\le\lVert(L_xf)*g_j-g_j\rVert_1+\lVert f*g_j-g_j\rVert_1<\varepsilon$ for every $x\in Q$. Since $Q$ and $\varepsilon$ were arbitrary, $G$ satisfies (P1). An amenable $G$ has a left-invariant mean on $L^\infty(G)$, whose restriction to the subspace $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ is a left-invariant mean there; hence (P1) holds.

items.title: A Reiter net has an invariant-mean cluster point
items.statement: Assume the ultrafilter lemma. Let $(f_i)$ be a Reiter net on $G$ and define $\lambda_{f_i}\in L^\infty(G)^*$ by $\lambda_{f_i}(\varphi)=\int_Gf_i\varphi\,d\mu$. Then the net $(\lambda_{f_i})$ has a weak-star cluster point $m$, and every such cluster point is a left-invariant mean on $L^\infty(G)$. Consequently Reiter's condition (P1) implies that $G$ is amenable ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]).
items.strategy: The functionals $\lambda_f$ lie in the dual unit ball by $|\lambda_f(\varphi)|\le\lVert f\rVert_1\lVert\varphi\rVert_\infty$, and the dual unit ball is weak-star compact by Banach-Alaoglu applied to the normed space $L^\infty(G)$; compactness yields a cluster point of the net. Positivity and $m(1_G)=1$ pass to limits because $\lambda_f(\varphi)\ge0$ for $\varphi\ge0$ and $\lambda_f(1_G)=\lVert f\rVert_1=1$ hold throughout. For invariance let $g\in G$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$: since $\lambda_f(L_g\varphi)=\int f\,(L_g\varphi)\,d\mu=\int(L_{g^{-1}}f)\varphi\,d\mu$, $|\lambda_f(L_g\varphi)-\lambda_f(\varphi)|\le\lVert L_{g^{-1}}f-f\rVert_1\lVert\varphi\rVert_\infty$, and Reiter's uniformity on the compact set $\{g^{-1},e\}$ makes this tend to zero; the same estimate with $g$ replaced by $g^{-1}$ handles $L_g$. Passing to the cluster point gives $m(L_g\varphi)=m(\varphi)$.

items.title: Amenability is equivalent to Reiter's condition (P1)
items.statement: Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group. Then $G$ is amenable ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]) if and only if $G$ satisfies Reiter's condition (P1) ([[def-reiter-condition-p1]]): for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $f\in L^1(G)$ with $f\ge0$, $\lVert f\rVert_1=1$ and $\sup_{x\in Q}\lVert L_xf-f\rVert_1\le\varepsilon$. The equivalence is proved through invariant means on $L^\infty(G)$, so it is stated for a fixed left Haar measure but does not depend on its normalization.
items.strategy: Assume AC (both directions route through choice-qualified lemmas). ($\Rightarrow$) If $G$ is amenable, restrict an invariant mean on $L^\infty(G)$ to the closed subspace $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ ([[def-left-uniformly-continuous-bounded-functions-on-a-locally-compact-group]]); the restriction is a positive unital functional and remains left-invariant, so [[lem-an-invariant-mean-produces-a-reiter-net]] yields (P1). ($\Leftarrow$) If (P1) holds, [[lem-a-reiter-net-has-an-invariant-mean-cluster-point]] produces a weak-star cluster point of the associated functionals, which is a left-invariant mean on $L^\infty(G)$; thus $G$ is amenable. Nets, not sequences, are used throughout, and no countability or unimodularity assumption enters.

items.title: Folner nets give Reiter nets
items.statement: Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$ and let $F\subseteq G$ be $\mu$-measurable with $0<\mu(F)<\infty$. Put $f_F:=\mu(F)^{-1}\mathbf 1_F\in L^1(G)$. Then $f_F\ge0$, $\lVert f_F\rVert_1=1$, and for every $x\in G$$$\lVert L_xf_F-f_F\rVert_1=\frac{\mu(xF\mathbin\triangle F)}{\mu(F)} .$$Consequently, if $(F_i)$ is a left Folner net ([[def-left-folner-net-for-a-locally-compact-group]]) then $(f_{F_i})$ is a Reiter net for $G$, and the left Folner condition implies Reiter's condition (P1) ([[def-reiter-condition-p1]]).
items.strategy: Left translation acts on indicators by $L_x\mathbf 1_F=\mathbf 1_{xF}$: $(L_x\mathbf 1_F)(y)=\mathbf 1_F(x^{-1}y)=\mathbf 1_{xF}(y)$. Hence $L_xf_F-f_F=\mu(F)^{-1}(\mathbf 1_{xF}-\mathbf 1_F)$ is a function of modulus $\mu(F)^{-1}$ exactly on the symmetric difference $xF\mathbin\triangle F$ and vanishes off it, so its $L^1$-norm and the first formula follow from the defining property of the integral of a simple function. Left invariance of the Haar measure gives $\mu(xF)=\mu(F)$, so $\lVert f_F\rVert_1=\mu(F)^{-1}\mu(F)=1$ and $f_F\in\mathcal P$; measurability of $xF$ is the translation invariance of the measure. Inserting the formula into the defining estimates of the left Folner condition gives the Reiter estimates for the same compact sets and tolerances, which is precisely the net formulation of (P1).

items.title: The layer-cake identity for integrable functions
items.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f,f'\in L^1(X)$ be nonnegative integrable functions (represented by fixed measurable functions). For $t\ge0$ put $E_t=\{f\ge t\}$ and $E'_t=\{f'\ge t\}$. Then $$\lVert f-f'\rVert_1=\int_0^\infty\mu(E_t\mathbin\triangle E'_t)\,dt ,$$and in particular $\lVert f\rVert_1=\int_0^\infty\mu(E_t)\,dt$. No $\sigma$-finiteness of $\mu$ is required: both sides only involve the $\sigma$-finite set $\{f>0\}\cup\{f'>0\}$.
items.strategy: For real $s,s'\ge0$ the elementary identity $|s-s'|=\int_0^\infty|\mathbf 1_{s\ge t}-\mathbf 1_{s'\ge t}|\,dt$ holds by splitting the integral at $s$ and $s'$. Applying it fibrewise gives $|f(x)-f'(x)|=\int_0^\infty|\mathbf 1_{E_t}(x)-\mathbf 1_{E'_t}(x)|\,dt$ for every $x$. The set $S:=\{f>0\}\cup\{f'>0\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}(\{f>1/n\}\cup\{f'>1/n\})$ is $\sigma$-finite because $\mu(\{f>1/n\})\le n\lVert f\rVert_1<\infty$, and $f=f'=0$ off $S$. Tonelli's theorem on the $\sigma$-finite product $S\times(0,\infty)$ therefore allows the interchange of the $x$- and $t$-integrations, and $\int_X|\mathbf 1_{E_t}-\mathbf 1_{E'_t}|\,d\mu=\mu(E_t\mathbin\triangle E'_t)$. For $t>0$ the set $E_t$ has $\mu(E_t)\le\lVert f\rVert_1/t<\infty$; the single value $t=0$ is immaterial for the Lebesgue integral in $t$.

items.title: Reiter functions can be cut down to Folner sets
items.statement: Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$, let $Q\subseteq G$ be compact with $\mu(Q)>0$, let $\varepsilon>0$, and let $f\in L^1(G)$ satisfy $f\ge0$, $\lVert f\rVert_1=1$ and $\sup_{x\in Q^2}\lVert L_xf-f\rVert_1\le\varepsilon\mu(Q)/(2\mu(Q^2))$, where $Q^2=\{xy:x,y\in Q\}$. Then there is a Borel set $U\subseteq G$ with $0<\mu(U)<\infty$ and $\sup_{x\in Q}\mu(xU\mathbin\triangle U)/\mu(U)\le2\varepsilon$. Consequently Reiter's condition (P1) implies the left Folner condition: for every compact $Q$ and every $\varepsilon$ a set $U$ with $\sup_{x\in Q}\mu(xU\mathbin\triangle U)/\mu(U)\le2\varepsilon$ exists.
items.strategy: Fix $f$ as in the statement and put $E_t:=\{f\ge t\}$ for $t\ge0$; these are Borel and $\mu(E_t)\le\lVert f\rVert_1/t$ is finite for $t>0$. By the layer-cake identity $\lVert L_xf-f\rVert_1=\int_0^\infty\mu(xE_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)\,dt$ for every $x$ (left invariance identifies $xE_t$ with the superlevel set of $L_xf$). Integrating the hypothesis over the compact set $K:=Q^2$ (finite Haar measure) and interchanging the two integrals by Tonelli on the $\sigma$-finite product $K\times(0,\infty)$ gives $\int_0^\infty\mu(E_t)\bigl(\int_K\mu(xE_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)/\mu(E_t)\,dx\bigr)dt=\int_K\lVert L_xf-f\rVert_1\,dx\le\varepsilon\mu(Q)/2$. Since $\int_0^\infty\mu(E_t)\,dt=\lVert f\rVert_1=1$, there exists $t$ with $0<\mu(E_t)<\infty$ and $\int_K\mu(xE_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)/\mu(E_t)\,dx\le\varepsilon\mu(Q)/2$ (otherwise the left side would exceed $\varepsilon\mu(Q)/2$). Let $A:=\{x\in K:\mu(xE_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)/\mu(E_t)\le\varepsilon\}$; by Markov's inequality $\mu(K\setminus A)\le\varepsilon^{-1}\int_{K\setminus A}\mu(xE_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)/\mu(E_t)\,dx<\mu(Q)/2$. For $x\in Q$ one has $xQ\subseteq xK\cap K$, so $\mu(Q)=\mu(xQ)\le\mu(xK\cap K)\le\mu(xA\cap A)+2\mu(K\setminus A)<\mu(xA\cap A)+\mu(Q)$, hence $xA\cap A\neq\varnothing$ and $x\in AA^{-1}$. Writing $x=x_1x_2^{-1}$ with $x_1,x_2\in A$ and using $x_1x_2^{-1}E_t\mathbin\triangle E_t\subseteq x_1(x_2^{-1}E_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)\cup(x_1E_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)$ together with left invariance gives $\mu(xE_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)\le\mu(x_2E_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)+\mu(x_1E_t\mathbin\triangle E_t)\le2\varepsilon\mu(E_t)$. Thus $U:=E_t$ has the required property. For the consequence, given an arbitrary compact $Q$ replace it by a compact set $Q_0\supseteq Q$ containing $e$ and a nonempty open set (a compact neighbourhood times $Q$); estimates uniform on $Q_0$ restrict to $Q$, and $\mu(Q_0)>0$ by positivity of Haar measure on nonempty open sets. Choosing $f$ by (P1) for the compact set $Q_0^2$ and the tolerance $\varepsilon\mu(Q_0)/(2\mu(Q_0^2))$ produces the Folner set for $Q$.

items.title: The Folner criterion for locally compact groups
items.statement: Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$. Then $G$ is amenable if and only if it satisfies the left Folner condition ([[def-left-folner-net-for-a-locally-compact-group]]): for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $\mu$-measurable $F\subseteq G$ with $0<\mu(F)<\infty$ and $\sup_{x\in Q}\mu(xF\mathbin\triangle F)/\mu(F)\le\varepsilon$. Equivalently, $G$ admits a left Folner net. Borel sets suffice for $F$.
items.strategy: Amenable $\Rightarrow$ (P1) ([[thm-amenability-is-equivalent-to-reiter-p1]]) $\Rightarrow$ Folner (the consequence in [[lem-reiter-functions-can-be-cut-down-to-folner-sets]], with the reduction of an arbitrary compact $Q$ to a compact set of positive measure containing $e$). Conversely the normalized indicators of a Folner net form a Reiter net ([[lem-folner-nets-give-reiter-nets]]), and (P1) $\Rightarrow$ amenable by [[thm-amenability-is-equivalent-to-reiter-p1]]. The passage from the single-set condition to the net formulation is the standard equivalence used in [[def-left-folner-net-for-a-locally-compact-group]], and the tolerance is free because $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary. Every step keeps the same fixed left Haar measure and left translates, so nonunimodular groups are not excluded.

items.title: Folner sequences for second countable compactly generated groups
items.statement: Let $G$ be a second countable compactly generated locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$ and a compact generating set $S=S^{-1}$ containing $e$ and a nonempty open set. Then there is a sequence $(F_n)_{n\ge1}$ of Borel sets with $0<\mu(F_n)<\infty$ such that for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ $$\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{x\in Q}\frac{\mu(xF_n\mathbin\triangle F_n)}{\mu(F_n)}=0 .$$ Such a sequence is a Folner sequence for $G$; only compact generation, not second countability, is used by the construction.
items.strategy: Put $K_n:=S^n$; each $K_n$ is compact (products of compact sets under the continuous multiplication) and, since $e\in\operatorname{int}S$, one has $S\subseteq\operatorname{int}(S)\cdot S\subseteq\operatorname{int}(S^2)$ and inductively $K_n\subseteq\operatorname{int}K_{n+1}$, with $\bigcup_nK_n=G$ because $S$ generates $G$. Given a compact $Q$, the increasing open cover $\{\operatorname{int}K_{n+1}\}_n$ of $Q$ has a finite subcover, so $Q\subseteq K_{n_0}$ for some $n_0$. Apply the Folner criterion ([[thm-folner-criterion-for-locally-compact-groups]]) to the compact set $K_n$ with tolerance $1/n$; this gives $F_n$ with $\sup_{x\in K_n}\mu(xF_n\mathbin\triangle F_n)/\mu(F_n)\le1/n$. For $n\ge n_0$ the supremum over $Q\subseteq K_n$ is bounded by the supremum over $K_n$, hence by $1/n\to0$. Since every compact set is contained in some $K_{n_0}$, the sequence is a Folner sequence.

items.title: The Hulanicki-Reiter weak containment criterion for amenability
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$, let $1_G$ be the trivial unitary representation on $\mathbb C$ and let $\lambda_G$ be the left regular representation ([[def-left-and-right-regular-unitary-representations]], [[thm-regular-representations-are-unitary-and-strongly-continuous]]). Then $G$ is amenable if and only if $1_G\prec\lambda_G$ (Definition [[def-weak-containment-of-unitary-representations]]). Equivalently, $G$ is amenable if and only if $\lambda_G$ almost has invariant unit vectors, i.e. for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a unit vector $\xi\in L^2(G)$ with $\sup_{x\in Q}\lVert\lambda_G(x)\xi-\xi\rVert_2<\varepsilon$.
items.strategy: ($\Rightarrow$) By [[thm-amenability-is-equivalent-to-reiter-p1]] fix, for compact $Q$ and $\varepsilon>0$, a density $f\in L^1(G)$ with $f\ge0$, $\lVert f\rVert_1=1$ and $\sup_{x\in Q}\lVert L_xf-f\rVert_1<\varepsilon$. Put $g:=\sqrt f\in L^2(G)$, so $\lVert g\rVert_2=1$. For nonnegative $a,b$ one has $|a-b|^2\le|a^2-b^2|$; hence $\lVert\lambda_G(x)g-g\rVert_2^2=\int_G|g(x^{-1}y)-g(y)|^2dy\le\int_G|g(x^{-1}y)^2-g(y)^2|dy=\lVert L_xf-f\rVert_1<\varepsilon$. Since $x\mapsto\langle\lambda_G(x)g,g\rangle$ is the coefficient of $\lambda_G$ at $g$ ([[def-matrix-coefficient-of-a-unitary-representation]]) and $|1-\langle\lambda_G(x)g,g\rangle|\le\lVert\lambda_G(x)g-g\rVert_2$ by Cauchy-Schwarz ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]), the constant function $1$ -- the coefficient of the trivial representation at the unit vector, and the only kind of positive-type function associated to $1_G$ -- is approximated uniformly on $Q$ by coefficients of $\lambda_G$, which is exactly $1_G\prec\lambda_G$. ($\Leftarrow$) If $1_G\prec\lambda_G$, [[lem-weak-containment-of-the-trivial-representation-and-almost-invariant-vectors]] (which uses AC) supplies for compact $Q$ and $\varepsilon>0$ a unit vector $\xi\in L^2(G)$ with $\sup_{x\in Q}\lVert\lambda_G(x)\xi-\xi\rVert_2<\varepsilon$. Put $f:=|\xi|^2\in L^1(G)$; then $f\ge0$, $\lVert f\rVert_1=\lVert\xi\rVert_2^2=1$ and, by Cauchy-Schwarz, $\lVert L_xf-f\rVert_1=\int_G||\xi(x^{-1}y)|^2-|\xi(y)|^2|dy\le\lVert\lambda_G(x)\xi+\xi\rVert_2\lVert\lambda_G(x)\xi-\xi\rVert_2\le2\lVert\lambda_G(x)\xi-\xi\rVert_2<2\varepsilon$. Thus (P1) holds, and [[thm-amenability-is-equivalent-to-reiter-p1]] gives amenability.

items.title: The Markov-Kakutani fixed point theorem for abelian affine actions
items.statement: Let $G$ be an abelian topological group acting on a nonempty compact convex subset $X$ of a locally convex topological vector space $V$ by an action $G\times X\to X$, $(g,x)\mapsto gx$ which is continuous and affine in $x$ (that is, $(gh)x=g(hx)$, $ex=x$, and $x\mapsto gx$ is continuous and affine for every $g$). Then the action has a fixed point: there is $x_0\in X$ with $gx_0=x_0$ for all $g\in G$.
items.strategy: For $n\ge0$ and $g\in G$ define the continuous affine map $A_n(g)x:=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{i=0}^ng^ix$; convexity of $X$ makes $A_n(g)$ a map $X\to X$. Let $\mathcal G$ be the semigroup of continuous affine maps of $X$ generated by $\{A_n(g)\}$; it is abelian because $A_n(g)A_m(h)=A_m(h)A_n(g)$ for commuting $g,h$. Each $\gamma(X)$ is compact, hence closed in $X$. The family $\{\gamma(X)\}_{\gamma\in\mathcal G}$ has the finite intersection property: for $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_k$ and $\gamma=\gamma_1\cdots\gamma_k$, commutativity writes $\gamma=\gamma_i\circ\gamma_i'$, so $\gamma(X)\subseteq\gamma_i(X)$ for every $i$, and $\gamma(X)\neq\varnothing$. Since $X$ is compact, the finite intersection property gives ([[thm-compact-iff-fip]]) a point $x_0\in\bigcap_{\gamma\in\mathcal G}\gamma(X)$. Fix $g\in G$ and $n\ge0$; by construction there is $x\in X$ with $x_0=A_n(g)x$. For every continuous linear functional $\varphi\in V^*$, $|\varphi(x_0-gx_0)|=\frac1{n+1}|\varphi(x)-\varphi(g^{n+1}x)|\le\frac{2C}{n+1}$ where $C=\sup_{y\in X}|\varphi(y)|<\infty$ by compactness. Letting $n\to\infty$ gives $\varphi(x_0-gx_0)=0$ for every $\varphi\in V^*$; since the continuous dual of a locally convex space separates points ([[thm-locally-convex-continuous-dual-separates-points]]), $x_0=gx_0$. As $g$ was arbitrary, $x_0$ is fixed by $G$.

items.title: The fixed point property implies amenability
items.statement: Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group such that every continuous affine action of $G$ on a nonempty compact convex subset of a locally convex topological vector space has a fixed point (the fixed point property). Then $G$ is amenable ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]).
items.strategy: Let $M$ be the set of means on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ ([[def-left-uniformly-continuous-bounded-functions-on-a-locally-compact-group]]): positive linear functionals $m$ with $m(1_G)=1$. Viewed in the weak-star topology on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)^*$, $M$ is nonempty (point evaluation at $e$), convex, and weak-star closed, because positivity and $m(1_G)=1$ are pointwise conditions; it is contained in the dual unit ball, which is weak-star compact by [[thm-banach-alaoglu]]. Hence $M$ is a compact convex subset of the locally convex space $\mathrm{UCB}(G)^*$ with the weak-star topology. The formula $(g\cdot m)(\varphi):=m(L_{g^{-1}}\varphi)$ defines an affine action of $G$ on $M$; it is continuous: for nets $g_i\to g$ and $m_i\to m$ and fixed $\varphi$, $|(g_i\cdot m_i)(\varphi)-(g\cdot m)(\varphi)|\le\lVert L_{g_i^{-1}}\varphi-L_{g^{-1}}\varphi\rVert_\infty+|(m_i-m)(L_{g^{-1}}\varphi)|\to0$, the first term by the defining translation-continuity of $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ and the second by weak-star convergence. The fixed point property therefore gives $m\in M$ with $g\cdot m=m$ for all $g$, i.e. $m(L_{g^{-1}}\varphi)=m(\varphi)$ for all $g,\varphi$: a left-invariant mean on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$. By [[lem-an-invariant-mean-produces-a-reiter-net]] it satisfies (P1), and [[lem-a-reiter-net-has-an-invariant-mean-cluster-point]] converts (P1) into a left-invariant mean on $L^\infty(G)$; hence $G$ is amenable.

items.title: Compact and locally compact abelian groups are amenable
items.statement: (1) Every compact locally compact Hausdorff group is amenable. (2) Every locally compact Hausdorff abelian group is amenable. No countability, metrizability or unimodularity hypothesis is imposed.
items.strategy: (1) Let $K$ be compact with normalized Haar probability $\mu$ ([[cor-normalized-haar-probability-on-a-compact-group]]). Define $m(\varphi):=\int_K\varphi\,d\mu$ for $\varphi\in L^\infty(K)$. Then $m$ is a positive $\mathbb C$-linear functional with $m(1_K)=1$ (so a mean), and $m(L_g\varphi)=\int_K\varphi(g^{-1}x)d\mu(x)=\int_K\varphi\,d\mu=m(\varphi)$ by left invariance of the Haar integral, for all $g\in K$. Hence $m$ is a left-invariant mean and $K$ is amenable. (2) Let $G$ be abelian. By [[lem-markov-kakutani-fixed-point-theorem-for-abelian-affine-actions]], every continuous affine action of the abelian group $G$ on a nonempty compact convex subset of a locally convex topological vector space has a fixed point; that is, $G$ has the fixed point property. By [[lem-a-group-with-the-fixed-point-property-is-amenable]], $G$ is amenable.

items.title: Amenability is stable under closed subgroups, quotients and extensions
items.statement: Let $G$ be an amenable locally compact Hausdorff group. Then: (i) every closed subgroup $H\le G$ is amenable; (ii) for every closed normal subgroup $N\trianglelefteq G$ the Hausdorff quotient $G/N$ is amenable; (iii) if $N\trianglelefteq G$ is closed normal, $N$ is amenable and $G/N$ is amenable, then $G$ is amenable.
items.strategy: Conventions: amenability is the existence of a left-invariant mean on $L^\infty$ ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]); via the restriction of such a mean to $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ and [[lem-an-invariant-mean-produces-a-reiter-net]], [[lem-a-reiter-net-has-an-invariant-mean-cluster-point]] and [[thm-amenability-is-equivalent-to-reiter-p1]], this is equivalent to the existence of an invariant mean on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$. (ii) Let $\pi:G\to G/N$ be the quotient map and let $m$ be an invariant mean on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$. For $\psi\in\mathrm{UCB}(G/N)$ the pullback $\psi\circ\pi$ lies in $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ because $L_{\bar g}\psi\circ\pi=L_g(\psi\circ\pi)$; the pullback is injective (and isometric) since $\pi$ is onto, and $m_{G/N}(\psi):=m(\psi\circ\pi)$ is a positive unital functional. If $\psi'=L_{\bar g}\psi$ then $\psi'\circ\pi=L_g(\psi\circ\pi)$, so invariance of $m$ gives $m_{G/N}(\psi')=m_{G/N}(\psi)$. Hence $G/N$ has an invariant mean on its UCB space and is amenable. (iii) Let $m_N$ and $m_{G/N}$ be invariant means on $\mathrm{UCB}(N)$ and $\mathrm{UCB}(G/N)$. For $\varphi\in\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ define $F(g):=m_N\bigl(h\mapsto\varphi(gh)\bigr)$; the function $h\mapsto\varphi(gh)$ lies in $\mathrm{UCB}(N)$ because $|\varphi(gh'h)-\varphi(gh)|\le\sup_x|\varphi(h'x)-\varphi(x)|$. Left invariance of $m_N$ gives $F(gn)=F(g)$ for $n\in N$, so $F=\psi\circ\pi$ for a unique $\psi:\,G/N\to\mathbb C$, and $\psi\in\mathrm{UCB}(G/N)$ because $|F(\gamma g)-F(g)|\le\sup_x|\varphi(\gamma x)-\varphi(x)|$ tends to $0$ uniformly. Set $m(\varphi):=m_{G/N}(\psi)$; this is positive and unital, and left invariance follows because $\varphi\mapsto\varphi\circ L_\gamma$ sends $F$ to $L_\gamma F$ and hence $\psi$ to $L_{\gamma N}\psi$, which $m_{G/N}$ cannot see. So $G$ has an invariant mean on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ and is amenable. (i) Escalated. The standard route is Hulanicki-Reiter: $1_G\prec\lambda_G$ restricts to $1_H\prec\lambda_G|_H$, and $\lambda_G|_H\prec\lambda_H$ (weak containment of the restricted left regular representation in the regular representation of a closed subgroup) gives $1_H\prec\lambda_H$; the proof of $\lambda_G|_H\prec\lambda_H$ in the source is exactly the quasi-invariant-measure and Weil-integration-formula computation for $G/H$. That computation is published in this library on the page `induced-unitary-representations-of-locally-compact-groups` (items `thm-existence-of-rho-functions-and-quasi-invariant-measures-on-g-mod-h` and `thm-weil-quotient-integration-formula-with-rho-function`), which is NOT in the transitive requires closure of this page, so no item of this page may depend on it without an owner decision. The exact missing supplier, placement and dependency chain are recorded in the batch notes. No other clause is affected.

title: Amenability Reiter Nets and Folner Conditions — Examples

items.title: Folner sets in R^n
items.statement: Let $G=\mathbb R^n$ be the additive group with its Euclidean topology and let $\mu=\lambda_n$ be Lebesgue measure. Then $\lambda_n$ is a left Haar measure on $G$, and the expanding cubes $C_t:=[-t,t]^n$, $t>0$, form a left Folner net: for every compact $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $Q\subseteq[-R,R]^n$ and every $t>0$, $$\sup_{x\in Q}\frac{\lambda_n(x+C_t\mathbin\triangle C_t)}{\lambda_n(C_t)}\le2\bigl((1+R/t)^n-1\bigr)\xrightarrow[t\to\infty]{}0 .$$ In particular $\mathbb R^n$ satisfies the left Folner condition ([[def-left-folner-net-for-a-locally-compact-group]]) and is amenable by [[thm-folner-criterion-for-locally-compact-groups]].
items.strategy: Lebesgue measure is translation invariant ([[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]], [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]), finite on compact sets, and it is a Radon measure ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-radon-measure-on-rn]]); translation invariance for the additive group is left invariance, and every translate of a Borel set is measurable. Hence $\lambda_n$ is a left Haar measure, and by uniqueness of Haar measure ([[thm-uniqueness-of-left-haar-measure-up-to-scale]]) every other left Haar measure on $\mathbb R^n$ is a positive multiple of it; the Folner ratio is scale-invariant, so it suffices to test with $\lambda_n$. For $x\in Q$ the symmetric difference $(x+C_t)\mathbin\triangle C_t$ is contained in the shell $S_{t,R}:=\{y:\max_j|y_j|\le t+R\}\setminus\{y:\max_j|y_j|<t\}$, and left invariance makes both sets of equal measure, so $\lambda_n((x+C_t)\mathbin\triangle C_t)\le2\lambda_n(S_{t,R})=2\bigl((2(t+R))^n-(2t)^n\bigr)$ by the box measure formula ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]) and additivity of Lebesgue measure on the disjoint pieces. Dividing by $\lambda_n(C_t)=(2t)^n$ gives the displayed bound, which tends to $0$ as $t\to\infty$ for fixed $R$; the resulting net indexed by $t\in(0,\infty)$ is therefore a left Folner net for $G$.

items.title: Compact groups have a constant Reiter net
items.statement: Let $K$ be a compact locally compact Hausdorff group with normalized Haar probability $\mu$, so $\mu(K)=1$, and let $f:=\mathbf 1_K\in L^1(K)$. Then $f\ge0$, $\lVert f\rVert_1=1$, and $L_xf=f$ for every $x\in K$, because $L_x\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_{xK}=\mathbf 1_K$. Hence the constant net $f_i:=f$ satisfies Reiter's condition (P1) exactly, with $\sup_{x\in Q}\lVert L_xf-f\rVert_1=0$ for every compact $Q\subseteq K$, and $K$ is amenable by [[thm-amenability-is-equivalent-to-reiter-p1]]. This is the strongest possible form of approximate invariance: the approximating densities do not vary with the tolerance.
items.strategy: Compactness makes $K$ a member of its own collection of compact subsets and $xK=K$ for every $x\in K$, so $L_x\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_{xK}=\mathbf 1_K$ as functions and as $L^1$-classes; the normalization $\lVert\mathbf 1_K\rVert_1=\mu(K)=1$ is the normalized Haar probability ([[cor-normalized-haar-probability-on-a-compact-group]]). The Reiter estimates hold with value $0$ for every compact $Q$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, so (P1) holds, and the Reiter equivalence theorem yields amenability. Note that the same computation shows directly that $m(\varphi)=\int_K\varphi\,d\mu$ is an invariant mean on $L^\infty(K)$, so the example also checks the compact case of [[prop-compact-and-locally-compact-abelian-groups-are-amenable]].

items.title: The real affine group is amenable and nonunimodular
items.statement: Let $G:=\{(a,b):a>0,\ b\in\mathbb R\}$ with the multiplication $(a,b)(a',b')=(aa',ab'+b)$ and the topology inherited from $\mathbb R^2$ (the $ax+b$ group, an open subset of $\mathbb R^2$ and hence locally compact Hausdorff). Then $G$ is amenable, but $G$ is not unimodular: with the left Haar measure $d\mu_L=a^{-2}\,da\,db$ one has $\Delta_G(a,b)=a^{-1}\ne1$, so amenability does not imply unimodularity.
items.strategy: The multiplication is smooth and makes $G$ a locally compact Hausdorff group with identity $(1,0)$ and inverse $(a,b)^{-1}=(a^{-1},-b/a)$; the subset $N:=\{(1,b):b\in\mathbb R\}$ is a closed normal abelian subgroup isomorphic to $(\mathbb R,+)$ with abelian quotient $G/N\cong\mathbb R_{>0}$ (the projection $(a,b)\mapsto a$). Amenability: let $G$ act continuously and affinely on a nonempty compact convex set $X$; since $\mathbb R\cong N$ is abelian, the Markov-Kakutani lemma ([[lem-markov-kakutani-fixed-point-theorem-for-abelian-affine-actions]]) gives an $N$-fixed point. The $N$-fixed set $X^N$ is nonempty, compact, convex and $G$-invariant (normality of $N$), and the $G$-action on it factors through the abelian group $G/N\cong\mathbb R_{>0}$, so a second application of Markov-Kakutani gives a point fixed by $G$. Thus $G$ has the fixed point property, and [[lem-a-group-with-the-fixed-point-property-is-amenable]] makes $G$ amenable. Nonunimodularity: $d\mu_L=a^{-2}da\,db$ is left invariant because $(a,b)\mapsto(a_0a,a_0b+b_0)$ has Jacobian $a_0^2$ and $a^{-2}$ acquires the factor $a_0^{-2}$; right translation by $(a',b')$ maps $(a,b)\mapsto(aa',ab'+b)$ with Jacobian $a'$ in the coordinates $(A,B)=(aa',ab'+b)$, and $A^{-2}dA\,dB=a'^{-1}a^{-2}da\,db$; hence the modular function ([[def-modular-function-of-a-locally-compact-group]], [[lem-right-translation-scales-left-haar-measure]]) is $\Delta_G(a',b')=a'^{-1}\neq1$, so $G$ is nonunimodular ([[def-unimodular-locally-compact-group]]).

items.title: The free group on two generators is not amenable
items.statement: Let $F_2=\langle a,b\rangle$ be the free group on two generators with the discrete topology and let $\mu$ be counting measure, a left Haar measure ([[lem-counting-measure-on-a-discrete-group]]). Then $F_2$ is not amenable: there is no left-invariant mean on $L^\infty(F_2,\mu)$ in the sense of [[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]. This is the standard nonamenable contrast for the page and matches the published discrete statement [[thm-free-group-of-rank-two-is-nonamenable]].
items.strategy: Because the topology is discrete, $\mu$ is counting measure, every function on $F_2$ is $\mu$-measurable and the only $\mu$-null set is $\varnothing$; hence $L^\infty(F_2,\mu)=\ell^\infty(F_2)$ literally, and a left-invariant mean in the sense of [[def-left-invariant-mean-on-l-infinity-of-a-locally-compact-group]] is exactly a left-invariant mean on $\ell^\infty(F_2)$ in the discrete sense of [[def-left-invariant-mean-and-amenable-group]]. Suppose such an $m$ exists. For a subset $A\subseteq F_2$ write $m(A):=m(\mathbf 1_A)$. Let $A$ be the set of reduced words beginning with a nonzero power of $a$ (including the empty word convention is immaterial); every element of $F_2$ is either in $A$ or of the form $a w$ with $w\in A$ wait, more precisely $F_2=A\sqcup aA$: a reduced word not beginning with a nonzero power of $a$ either is empty or begins with a nonzero power of $b$, and then its image under multiplication by $a$ on the left begins with $a$, so it lies in $A$; conversely $aA\subseteq F_2$. Hence $1=m(F_2)=m(A)+m(aA)=2m(A)$ by left invariance, so $m(A)=1/2$. On the other hand $A,bA,b^2A$ are pairwise disjoint subsets of $F_2$ (their elements begin with a nonzero power of $a$, of $b$, and of $b$ respectively, with the $b$-leading sets distinguished by the second letter), so $1=m(F_2)\ge m(A)+m(bA)+m(b^2A)=3m(A)=3/2$, a contradiction. Therefore no left-invariant mean exists and $F_2$ is not amenable.
